headline: Crime SuspenStories #22 heads to auction
post:
Remember the 1950s moral panic that changed the entire comic book industry? According to ComicBook.com, a particularly infamous piece of history is heading to the auction block just in time for Halloween. The issue in question is E.C.’s Crime SuspenStories #22. It features a cover with a killer holding an axe and a severed head, which was famously brought up during the 1954 Senate hearings on juvenile delinquency. Parents of the era routinely threw these graphic horror and crime books in the trash, making surviving copies surprisingly rare. Because angry parents destroyed so many copies back then, bidding has already climbed past $2k through Heritage. That intense controversy ultimately birthed the Comics Code Authority and reshaped publishers like Marvel and DC for decades to come. Would you add this piece of horror history to your collection?

#ComicBookHistory #HorrorComics #RetroCollectibles
original_title: This Gruesome 1950s Comic Cover Helped Spark a National Moral Panic (And Changed Comics Forever)

headline: Blake Crouch talks Dark Matter and Marvel
post:
Blake Crouch reportedly feels that blockbusters like "Avengers: Endgame" and "Spider-Man: No Way Home" mostly use alternate realities as an excuse to smash action figures together. According to /Film, the creator explained that he does not have "an extraordinary amount of respect" for that approach. Instead, his Apple TV series focuses on exploring character depths.

While blockbusters lean into nostalgia, this sci-fi story serves as a cautionary tale. Joel Edgerton and Dayo Okeniyi star in the series, which approaches infinite worlds through a darker lens. Crouch shared that his work treats the concept very differently than big studios do. 🌌

Do you prefer character-driven multiverse stories or action-packed team-ups? #DarkMatter #AppleTV #SciFi
original_title: Dark Matter Creator Doesn't Have 'Respect' For Marvel's Multiversal Storytelling [Exclusive]

post:
